# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 2
**Agent:** LOGOS (Formal Equivalence)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 2

---

1. We, the apostles, said to him: "Lord, tell us what is to come — what we will see. How are we to understand the resurrection of the dead? For you speak of great and marvelous things."

2. The Lord showed us a great garden, full of beautiful trees and blessed fruits, and of the fragrance of perfumes. The fragrance was pleasant, and its scent reached us as well.

3. He showed me also an aged man, gleaming in whiteness, and said to me: "This is how it will be at the hour of their need."

4. I, Peter, answered him: "What is it that you are saying? Who is this aged man, and who are the children? And what is this place?"

5. He said to me: "This garden and the trees that you see — these are the righteous dead. And the beautiful things you see here represent those who died for the sake of righteousness.

6. The aged man whom you saw — he is Moses, and the law which God gave him on Mount Sinai.

7. The children are those who died young before they had committed sin, who had not yet grown to full age. Since this is so, they are under the care of God."

8. He said: "I will show you another mystery. On the day when God judges the world, the righteous will stand before him, and the sinners will be on his left.

9. But some of the righteous will shine and some will not shine, for some have sinned and some have not."

10. I said to him: "I do not understand this. Please explain it to me."

11. He said: "Those who shine are those who have not sinned and have done the will of God. Those who do not shine are those who sinned but repented at the end.

12. Some of the righteous were poor in this world for God's sake; some fasted unto God; some prayed without ceasing; some gave freely of their possessions.

13. All these things will be revealed at the resurrection, according to God's will.

14. They will receive the kingdom, the honor, and the glory that God has prepared for those who have feared him."

---
*LOGOS note: Ethiopic text governs this chapter. The aged man as Moses is explicitly interpreted within the text — no external gloss added.*
